_readme: Operator-editable registry of Zo BYOK model configs for the MoA/consensus-gate catalogs. There is no server-side listing API for BYOK configs (frontend-session only), so UUIDs are recorded here manually. To add a model: Settings → AI → Models, copy the config UUID into `id` as `byok:<uuid>`, then run `bun catalog-byok.ts --refresh`. Entries with `id: null` are known-pending — the model exists in the Zo UI but its UUID has not been captured yet. `subscription: true` = flat-rate subscription billing (Claude Code / Codex), which is why these take precedence over usage-billed Opencode/OpenRouter in lineup selection.

models.label: Synthetic GLM-5.2
models.note: Synthetic.new, usage-billed (not a flat-rate Claude Code/Codex subscription). Factory /zo/ask failover rung 3 (operator-set 2026-07-10 — demoted off primary because it is persistently quota-429'd; Fable 5 is now primary). Probed like every other rung; while 429-capped deriveChain() further demotes it below Haiku to the tail until its quota clears.

models.label: Codex GPT 5.3 Codex
models.pending: Not registerable via the Codex subscription — Codex retired the gpt-5.3-codex slug. Config byok:a793ecfe-e6fa-4fcb-8b97-8cf4245065f0 EXISTS and resolves, but /zo/ask returns HTTP 502 "Couldn't switch to the model gpt-5.3-codex (Invalid params -32602)" because the upstream no longer serves it; ~/.codex/models_cache.json lists 8 slugs and gpt-5.3-codex is not among them (gpt-5.3-codex-spark is, but supported_in_api=false). Do not re-capture a Codex UUID — it will fail the same way. To route this model through BYOK, register an OpenAI API-key config (Settings → AI → Providers → Bring Your Own Key) rather than a Codex config; OpenRouter serves openai/gpt-5.3-codex with provider=OpenAI, so the API exposes it. Until then oc:gpt-5.3-codex and openai/gpt-5.3-codex are the only live routes (both verified 2026-07-27).
